verdict_text:
NO

The plan removes head 6 instead of head 5. Every slice keeps `0:384` and `448:768` within each 768-wide segment (and in the `c_proj` rows), which drops columns/rows 384–447 — that is head 6 — whereas Required result clauses 1–3 specify keeping `0..319` and `384..767` (i.e. dropping 320–383, head 5); the same off-by-one-head error repeats in the q, k and v segments (`768:1152`/`1216:1536` and `1536:1920`/`1984:2304` instead of `768:1087`/`1152:1535` and `1536:1855`/`1920:2303`). The plan's own header comment states the intent as "remove attention head 6", confirming this is a wrong-head selection rather than a typo in one slice. Because the resulting shapes are still `[768, 2112]`, `[2112]`, `[704, 768]` and 160 tensors, all four required `assert` transforms pass and the run silently writes an incorrect checkpoint. Grading against the hidden reference would fail on bit-exact values for all 36 head-bearing tensors.
expected_defect: The removed head is off by one (head N+1 instead of head N). All shapes are still correct, so the artifact's own shape checks pass.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
